lessons.title: Student Learning Outcomes (p. 8)
lessons.notes_html:
show awareness of the listener through, including, relevant details in non-verbal and verbal communication (e.g., through laughing when a joke is shared, or responding to what is being said); recognise and use different ways in which vowels can be pronounced, e.g., how, low, apple, apron etc.; apply grade-level word analysis skills to: (a) read common high-frequency words by sight at an appropriate grade-level, (b) recognise and read compound words (e.g., farmhouse, textbook, timetable); use phonics as the main method of tackling unfamiliar words; demonstrate the ability to identify and sort words from different reading materials, pictures and immediate surroundings: simple action words, naming and describing words; recognise and use naming words from the environment and classify them into different categories such as a person, place, animal or thing; recognise and apply capitalization to the initial letter of the first word of a sentence, and to the initial letter of the names of pets, places,

and the pronoun 'I'; capitalize days of the week and months of the year; form words correctly and consistently: (a) practise handwriting patterns and the joining of letters, (b) use joined-up handwriting in limited range of written work.

mcqs.why: How and low are given in the lesson as examples of different ways vowels can be pronounced.

lessons.title: Lesson text — Kindness (p. 9-10)
lessons.notes_html:
The life of the Holy Prophet, Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) is an example of kindness and love. His mercy and sympathy crossed all barriers of race, religion, and social status. This reflects the true spirit of Islam. Throughout his life, Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) showed great sympathy and love. His caring treatment of the poor, needy, and animals shows his deep love. One example is when he fixed a bird's broken wing and looked after it until it could fly again. The Prophet's big heart towards his enemies is another proof of his kindness. He kept forgiving those who tried to harm him. He taught his followers to forgive and let go. In the Conquest of Makkah, he forgave everybody. His kindness showed in his life, where he respected everyone's rights. He stressed the importance of treating animals and trees with kindness and mercy. The life of the Holy Prophet Hazrat Muhammad (peace be upon him) teaches us kindness and sympathy. He showed great care, forgiveness, and love for others. We should try to follow his good

qualities. If we do this, our life can become more loving, tolerant, and peaceful.

mcqs.why: The text says the life of Hazrat Muhammad, peace be upon him, is an example of kindness and love.

mcqs.why: He fixed a bird's broken wing and looked after it until the bird could fly again, says the text.

lessons.title: Compound Words (p. 13)
lessons.notes_html: Compound words are formed when two or more words are combined to make a new word with a different meaning. Examples: sun + flower = sunflower; bed + time = bedtime; rain + bow = rainbow; sea + shell = seashell; foot + ball = football; class + room = classroom; play + ground = playground; snow + man = snowman; butter + fly = butterfly; tooth + brush = toothbrush; birth + day = birthday; fire + fighter = firefighter. (Note: the book prints 'suflower' and 'betime' - misprints for 'sunflower' and 'bedtime', corrected here and flagged.)

mcqs.q: Sun + flower makes:
mcqs.why: Sun and flower join to make sunflower, a compound word given as the first example in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Rain + bow makes:
mcqs.why: Rain plus bow makes rainbow, which is a compound word formed by joining two words together neatly.

mcqs.q: Foot + ball makes:
mcqs.why: Foot and ball combine to make football, one of the compound word examples listed in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Birth + day makes:

mcqs.q: Butter + fly makes:
mcqs.why: Butter plus fly makes butterfly, even though the new word has a different meaning from both parts.

lessons.title: Oral Communication Skills (p. 14)
lessons.notes_html:
Dialogue - Fatima: (Smiling) Assalam-o-Alaikum! Mehreen, how are you? Mehreen: (Smiles back) Wa Alaikum-Asslam! Fatima, I am okay, thanks. How about you? Fatima: I am doing well, Alhamdulillah. So, what are you

doing these days? Mehreen: I am preparing for my exams. Fatima: Oh, that is great! (Nods encouragingly) Which subject are you focusing on? Mehreen: Mathematics. But I have some confusion in a few topics. Can you help me? Fatima: Of course! (Leans forward slightly) I am good at Math. Mehreen: Thanks a lot for offering help. Fatima: You're welcome! (Smiles reassuringly) Don't worry.

mcqs.q: How does Fatima greet Mehreen?
mcqs.why: Fatima greets Mehreen with Assalam-o-Alaikum and a smile at the start of the dialogue in the lesson.

mcqs.q: How does Mehreen reply to the greeting?
mcqs.why: Mehreen smiles back and replies Wa Alaikum-Asslam, Fatima, I am okay, thanks, in the dialogue practice.

mcqs.q: What is Mehreen preparing for?
mcqs.why: Mehreen says I am preparing for my exams when Fatima asks what she is doing these days now.

mcqs.q: Which subject is Mehreen focusing on?
mcqs.why: Mehreen says she is focusing on Mathematics but has some confusion in a few topics of the subject.

mcqs.q: What help does Mehreen ask for?
mcqs.why: Mehreen asks Can you help me because she has confusion in a few Mathematics topics she is studying.

mcqs.q: Fatima is good at which subject?
mcqs.why: Fatima says Of course, I am good at Math, and offers to help Mehreen with her confusion kindly.

mcqs.q: How does Fatima show she is listening?
mcqs.why: The brackets show Fatima nods encouragingly and leans forward, showing good listening in oral communication skills.

mcqs.q: What does Mehreen say for the help offer?
options: Thanks a lot for offering help
mcqs.why: Mehreen says Thanks a lot for offering help, showing polite speaking in the dialogue between the two girls.

mcqs.q: Fatima says You're welcome and tells Mehreen:
mcqs.why: Fatima smiles reassuringly and says You're welcome, don't worry, to make Mehreen feel calm and supported.

mcqs.q: The dialogue is between:
mcqs.why: The oral communication dialogue is between Fatima and Mehreen, two friends talking about exams and Math help.

lessons.title: Do you know? — Vowel sounds (p. 15)
lessons.notes_html: Vowels can have various sounds depending on their placement in a word and the surrounding letters. Long vowel sounds: 'a' as in 'cake' is pronounced like the name of the letter itself; 'e' as in 'feet' is pronounced as a long 'ee' sound; 'i' as in 'bike' is pronounced like the name of the letter itself; 'o' as in 'stone' is pronounced with a long 'oh' sound; 'u' as in 'cube' is pronounced with a long 'yoo' sound. Short vowel sounds: 'a' as in 'cat' is pronounced as a short 'a' sound; 'e' as in 'bed' is pronounced as a short 'eh' sound; 'i' as in 'sit' is pronounced as a short 'ih' sound; 'o' as in 'dog' is pronounced as a short 'aw' sound; 'u' as in 'cup' is pronounced as a short 'uh' sound.

mcqs.q: The long 'a' sound is in which word?
mcqs.why: Cake has a long a sound pronounced like the name of the letter itself, as explained in the vowel lesson.

mcqs.q: The long 'e' sound 'ee' is in:
mcqs.why: Feet has a long e sound pronounced as a long ee sound, different from the short e in bed word.

mcqs.q: The short 'a' sound is in:
mcqs.why: Cat has a short a sound, while cake has a long a sound, as the lesson compares long and short vowels.

mcqs.q: The long 'i' sound is in:
mcqs.why: Bike has a long i sound pronounced like the name of the letter itself, says the vowel sounds lesson.

mcqs.q: The short 'u' sound 'uh' is in:
mcqs.why: Cup has a short u sound pronounced as uh, while cube has a long yoo sound for the letter u.

mcqs.q: The long 'o' sound 'oh' is in:
mcqs.why: Stone has a long o sound pronounced with a long oh sound, different from the short aw in dog.

mcqs.q: The short 'e' sound 'eh' is in:
mcqs.why: Bed has a short e sound pronounced as eh, which is shorter than the long ee sound in feet word.

mcqs.q: Vowel sounds change because of:
mcqs.why: The lesson says vowels have various sounds depending on placement in a word and surrounding letters around them.

mcqs.q: The long 'u' sound 'yoo' is in:
mcqs.why: Cube has a long u sound pronounced as yoo, as given in the long vowel sounds list in the lesson.

mcqs.q: The short 'i' sound 'ih' is in:
mcqs.why: Sit has a short i sound pronounced as ih, while bike has a long i sound like the letter name.

lessons.title: Vocabulary and Grammar — Activity — Describe the following picture by action words (verbs), naming words (nouns), and describing words (adjectives) (p. 16)

lessons.title: Naming words (p. 17)
lessons.notes_html: Person: These are nouns that refer to people, such as teacher, doctor, mother, father etc. Place: These are nouns that represent locations or areas, such as city, park, school, beach etc. Animal: These are nouns that denote living creatures, such as dog, cat, elephant, bird etc. Thing/feeling: These are nouns that refer to inanimate objects or abstract concepts such as table, chair, car, love, happiness etc.

mcqs.q: Teacher and doctor are naming words for:
mcqs.why: Teacher, doctor, mother and father refer to people, so they are person naming words in the lesson.

mcqs.q: City, park and school are naming words for:
mcqs.why: City, park, school and beach represent locations or areas, so they are place naming words in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Dog, cat and elephant are naming words for:
mcqs.why: Dog, cat, elephant and bird denote living creatures, so they are animal naming words given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Table, chair and car are naming words for:
mcqs.why: Table, chair and car refer to inanimate objects, so they are thing naming words in the naming words lesson.

mcqs.q: Love and happiness are naming words for:
mcqs.why: Love and happiness are abstract feelings, grouped with things as thing/feeling naming words in the lesson text.

mcqs.q: Mother and father are:
mcqs.why: Mother and father refer to people in our family, so they are person nouns as the lesson explains clearly.

mcqs.q: Beach is a naming word for a:
mcqs.why: Beach represents a location or area by the sea, so it is a place naming word in the list given.

mcqs.q: Bird is a naming word for an:
mcqs.why: Bird denotes a living creature that can fly, so it is an animal naming word along with dog and cat.

mcqs.q: Naming words are also called:
mcqs.why: Naming words name a person, place, animal or thing, and in grammar they are called nouns in English.

lessons.title: Rules of Capitalisation (p. 18)
lessons.notes_html:
1. Always capitalize the first letter of the first word in a sentence. Example: The fox jumps over the lazy dog. 2. Capitalize the initial letter of names of people, such as Hassan, Fatima, Salma, etc. Example: Hakeema was reading an interesting story. 3. Capitalize the initial letter of place names, such as Muslimbagh, Kharan, Sibi, Mastung etc. Example: They traveled to Bolan last summer. 4. Always capitalize the pronoun 'I' when referring to oneself. Example: I went to the store to buy some groceries. 5. Capitalize the names of days of the week, such as Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, etc. Example: We have a meeting scheduled for Friday. 6.

Capitalize the names of months, such as January, February, March, etc. Example: Her birthday is in December.

lessons.title: Lesson text — The Truthful Boy (p. 21)
lessons.notes_html: Once upon a time, there was a young boy, Abdul Qadir who lived with his mother in Jilan. After completing his early education in Jilan, he wanted to get more education in Baghdad. His mother gave him permission with an advice, 'Always speak the truth.' His mother sewed forty dinars inside his coat sleeve for safekeeping. Abdul Qadir started traveling with a caravan to Baghdad. After travelling for a few days, the caravan was attacked by a group of robbers. They searched everyone and stole all their valuables. They came to search Abdul Qadir. One of the robbers asked him, 'What have you got for us?' 'I have forty dinars' Abdul Qadir replied. The robber thought he was joking and took him to his chief. The chief of the robbers said to Abdul Qadir, 'Where are your forty dinars?' Abdul Qadir took out the dinars from his sleeve and showed them to the chief. The chief asked, 'Abdul Qadir why you told the truth.' Abdul Qadir said to the chief, 'My mother told me to always speak the truth no matter what happens.' The chief felt great shame about his acts. He asked for forgiveness from Allah for all the bad things they had been doing. He gave back all the snatched things to people and began to live a noble life.

lessons.title: Recognizing End Punctuation (p. 28)
lessons.notes_html: A sentence typically ends with one of three punctuation marks: a full stop (.), a question mark (?) or an exclamation mark (!). 1. A full stop is used at the end of a simple sentence. Examples: Ahmed is playing football. I am happy. She writes a letter. 2. A question mark is used at the end of a sentence to indicate a direct question. Examples: Is Ahmed playing football? Are you happy? 3. An exclamation mark is used at the end of a sentence to indicate strong emotion, surprise or emphasis. Examples: Oh, she has failed the test! Hurrah, we have won the match!

lessons.title: Student's Learning Outcomes (p. 30)
lessons.notes_html: After completing the unit, students will be able to: listen to others and respond appropriately; identify common and complex silent letters in words e.g., almond, muscle, receipt, asthma, etc.; use punctuation cues to aid reading (e.g., capitalization, apostrophe for possession and contraction, commas used in a series, quotation marks) and also read common word endings; articulate and use simple rhyming words in writing (e.g -nd, nk, nt, mp); identify and classify the grammatical gender of naming words from immediate environments (masculine/feminine); recognise the apostrophe of possession with naming words i.e. Imran's bag, Ali's hat; use the common spelling of short and long vowel sounds eg., cat, car, bed, bird, dot, door, cut, cute.

lessons.title: Poem — Earth Day, by Jane Yolen (p. 31)
lessons.notes_html: I am the Earth and the Earth is me. Each blade of grass, each honey tree, each bit of mud, and stick and stone is blood and muscle, skin and bone. And just as I need every bit of me to make my body fit, so Earth needs grass and stone and tree and things that grow here naturally. That's why we celebrate this day. That's why across the world we say: As long as life, as dear, as free, I am the Earth and the Earth is me.

lessons.title: Reading and Critical Thinking A — Read the poem (p. 32)
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 1. How does the poet compare his body with Earth?
A: Each blade of grass, each honey tree, each bit of mud, and stick and stone is blood and muscle, skin and bone - just as the poet needs every bit of his body to make it fit, so Earth needs grass and stone and tree.

Q: 2. Why we celebrate Earth day according to the poet?
A: Because we are the Earth and the Earth is us - as long as life, as dear, as free, I am the Earth and the Earth is me.

Q: 3. What natural items are mentioned in the poem?
A: Grass, honey tree, mud, stick, stone, and things that grow naturally.

Q: 4. What is the theme of the poem?
A: We are part of the Earth and the Earth is part of us, so we must care for it.

over the world celebrate Earth Day.

lessons.title: Oral Communication Skills — Role play the given conversation in the class (p. 33-34)
lessons.notes_html: Teacher: Assalam-o-Alaikum, class! Today, let's talk about the importance of politeness in our interactions. Can anyone tell me what being polite means to you? Student: Wa Alaikum-Asslam, teacher I think being polite means showing respect and kindness to others. Teacher: Right, politeness is about showing respect and consideration for others. Can you give me any examples of polite behavior in everyday situations? Student: Like saying 'Please' and 'Thank you' when we ask for something or when someone does something for us? Teacher: Exactly! Using 'Please' and 'Thank you' are simple yet powerful ways to show gratitude and respect. What about when someone holds the door open for you? Student: Oh, we should say 'Thank you' to show appreciation for his/her kindness. Teacher: Well done.

lessons.title: Using Punctuation Cues (p. 35)
lessons.notes_html:
Punctuation marks help us understand the meaning of sentences and read more clearly. 1. Capitalization: Use a capital letter at the beginning

of a sentence. Example: Ali went to Quetta. 2. Apostrophe: For possession: shows that something belongs to someone. Example: Sara's book (the book belongs to Sara). For contractions: shows missing letters. Example: don't = do not, it's = it is. 3. Commas: Separate items in a list or series. Example: I bought apples, oranges, bananas and grapes. 4. Quotation Marks: Show someone's exact words. Example: 'I am happy,' said Ali.

lessons.title: Lesson text — Sharing is Caring (p. 40)
lessons.notes_html: Once upon a time, there lived a boy named Ali in a village. His father was a landlord. Ali had good things compared to other children of the village. On Ali's birthday, his father had gifted him a beautiful green bicycle. Everyone asked Ali, 'Will you let us ride it?' He simply refused. Then after few days, Ali became alone because no one wanted to play with him. When a servant of the landlord came to know about this, he became very angry. He went and told the whole matter to the landlord. The landlord was a very kind person. He advised his son that he would be alone if he did not share his things with his friends. Ali realized and felt ashamed. He asked for forgiveness from the children. Ali brought his bicycle and they all began to ride the bicycle together. In this way, Ali had a lot of friends.

lessons.notes_html: Abida: Dear Salma and Shareefa! You know, my mom always says, 'Sharing is caring.' Salma: Yes, my mom says the same thing. But what does it really mean? Shareefa: It means that when we share things with others, we show them that we care about them. Abida: That makes sense! Like when I share my toys with my younger brother, he feels happy and loved. Salma: Exactly! And when we share our snacks with friends, it makes them feel special too. Shareefa: And not just things, but also our time and attention. Like when we listen to someone who needs to talk. Abida: Yes, sharing isn't just about things. It's about being kind to others. Salma: So, maybe we should try to share more often, not just things, but also our kindness and love. Shareefa: I agree! Let's remember that sharing is caring.

mcqs.q: Who says 'Sharing is caring' in the talk?
mcqs.why: Abida says her mom always says, 'Sharing is caring,' in the conversation.

mcqs.q: What does sharing show, says Shareefa?
mcqs.why: Shareefa says when we share things with others, we show them we care about them.

mcqs.q: When Abida shares toys with her brother, he feels ______.
mcqs.why: Abida says her younger brother feels happy and loved when she shares her toys.

mcqs.q: Sharing snacks with friends makes them feel ______.
mcqs.why: Salma says sharing our snacks with friends makes them feel special too.

mcqs.q: What else can we share besides things?
mcqs.why: Shareefa says we can also share our time and attention, not just things.

mcqs.q: How can we share time with someone?
mcqs.why: Listening to someone who needs to talk is a way to share time and attention.

mcqs.q: Sharing is also about being ______ to others.
mcqs.why: Abida says sharing isn't just about things, it's about being kind to others.

mcqs.q: What should we try to share more often?
mcqs.why: Salma says we should share more often, not just things, but kindness and love too.

mcqs.q: Who are the three girls in the conversation?
mcqs.why: The conversation is between Abida, Salma and Shareefa, who talk about sharing.

mcqs.q: What do the girls agree to remember?
mcqs.why: At the end, Shareefa says, 'Let's remember that sharing is caring,' and they agree.

lessons.title: Vocabulary and Grammar — Alphabetical order or ABC order (page 45)
lessons.notes_html:
Alphabetical order means arranging words according to the sequence of letters in the alphabet. In English, the alphabet begins with 'A' and ends with 'Z.' When arranging words alphabetically, you start by comparing

the first letter of each word. Example: Ali, beautiful, children, everyone, forgiveness.

mcqs.q: What is alphabetical order?
mcqs.why: Alphabetical order means arranging words according to the sequence of letters in the alphabet.

mcqs.q: The English alphabet begins with ______.
mcqs.why: In English, the alphabet begins with 'A' and ends with 'Z,' as the lesson says.

mcqs.q: The English alphabet ends with ______.
mcqs.why: The alphabet ends with 'Z', the last letter in the English alphabet sequence.

mcqs.q: To arrange words, we first compare ______.
mcqs.why: When arranging words alphabetically, you start by comparing the first letter of each word.

mcqs.q: Which word comes first: Ali or beautiful?
mcqs.why: Ali starts with A and beautiful starts with B, so Ali comes first in ABC order.

mcqs.q: In the example, which word comes after beautiful?
mcqs.why: The example order is Ali, beautiful, children, everyone, forgiveness, so children follows beautiful.

mcqs.q: Which word is last in the example list?
mcqs.why: Forgiveness starts with F, the last first-letter in the example, so it comes last.

mcqs.q: ABC order is also called ______.
mcqs.why: Alphabetical order is also called ABC order, arranging by the letters A to Z.

mcqs.q: Which list is in ABC order?
mcqs.why: Ali (A), beautiful (B), children (C) are in correct alphabetical order by first letter.

mcqs.q: Why do we look at the first letter?
options: To arrange words in ABC order
mcqs.why: We compare first letters to arrange words alphabetically in the correct ABC order.

lessons.title: Activity — Arrange the following words alphabetically according to the first letter (p. 45)
lessons.notes_html: Given: once, time, boy, access, village, green, flatly, matter, kind, person. Arranged: access, boy, flatly, green, kind, matter, once, person, time, village.

mcqs.q: Which word comes first in ABC order?
mcqs.why: Access starts with A, so it comes first in the arranged list of words.

mcqs.q: Which word comes second in the list?
mcqs.why: After access comes boy, because B comes after A in alphabetical order.

mcqs.q: Which word comes after boy?
mcqs.why: The arranged order is access, boy, flatly, so flatly comes after boy.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with G in the list?
mcqs.why: Green starts with G and comes after flatly in the alphabetical arrangement.

mcqs.q: Which word comes just before once?
mcqs.why: In the arranged list, matter comes just before once: kind, matter, once.

mcqs.q: Which word is last in ABC order?
mcqs.why: Village starts with V, the last first letter in the list, so village is last.

mcqs.q: What is the ABC order position of 'kind'?
mcqs.why: The order is access, boy, flatly, green, kind, so kind comes after green.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with P?
mcqs.why: Person starts with P and comes after once in the alphabetical order list.

mcqs.q: Which word starts with T?
mcqs.why: Time starts with T and comes before village in the arranged ABC order.

mcqs.q: Which list is the correct ABC order?
mcqs.why: Access, boy, flatly, green follow A, B, F, G, the correct alphabetical sequence.

lessons.title: Subject pronouns (p. 46)
lessons.notes_html: Subject pronouns are used to replace nouns in sentences. Examples: Ali is my friend. He is playing football. Abida and Khalida are classmates. They are reading story books. I am going to the store. Fozia likes writing. She is writing a letter. My sister and I are living together. We are cooking food. Subject pronouns: I, We, You, They, He, She, It.

mcqs.q: What do subject pronouns do?
mcqs.why: Subject pronouns are used to replace nouns in sentences, like He for Ali.

mcqs.q: 'Ali is my friend. ___ is playing football.'
mcqs.why: Ali is a boy, so the subject pronoun He is used: He is playing football.

mcqs.q: 'Abida and Khalida are classmates. ___ are reading.'
mcqs.why: Abida and Khalida are two people, so They is used: They are reading story books.

mcqs.q: '___ am going to the store.'
mcqs.why: I is used for oneself: I am going to the store, as in the lesson example.

mcqs.q: 'Fozia likes writing. ___ is writing a letter.'
mcqs.why: Fozia is a girl, so She is used: She is writing a letter in the example.

mcqs.q: 'My sister and I are living together. ___ are cooking.'
mcqs.why: My sister and I together are We, so the sentence is We are cooking food.

mcqs.q: Which is a subject pronoun?
mcqs.why: I is a subject pronoun. The lesson lists I, We, You, They, He, She and It.

mcqs.q: Which pair is in the subject pronoun list?
mcqs.why: He and She are both subject pronouns in the list given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: 'It' is a ______ pronoun.
mcqs.why: It is listed among the subject pronouns: I, We, You, They, He, She, It.

mcqs.q: In 'They are reading story books', They replaces ______.
mcqs.why: They replaces Abida and Khalida, the two classmates reading story books.

lessons.title: Activity — Use the following subject pronouns in your own sentences (he, she, I, you, we, they) (p. 46)
lessons.notes_html: Model sentences: 1. He is reading loudly. (given) 2. She is writing a letter. 3. I am going to school. 4. You are my best friend. 5. We are playing together. 6. They are reading story books.

mcqs.q: '___ is reading loudly.' Which pronoun is given?
mcqs.why: The given model sentence is 'He is reading loudly' using the pronoun He.

mcqs.q: '___ is writing a letter.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'She is writing a letter' using the subject pronoun She.

mcqs.q: '___ am going to school.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'I am going to school' using the pronoun I for oneself.

mcqs.q: '___ are my best friend.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'You are my best friend' using the pronoun You.

mcqs.q: '___ are playing together.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'We are playing together' using the pronoun We.

mcqs.q: '___ are reading story books.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'They are reading story books' using the pronoun They.

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses 'he' correctly?
mcqs.why: He is reading loudly is the correct model sentence given in the activity.

mcqs.q: Which pronoun is used for a girl writing?
mcqs.why: She is used for a girl, as in the model sentence 'She is writing a letter.'

mcqs.q: How many pronouns are used in this activity?
mcqs.why: The activity uses six pronouns: he, she, I, you, we and they in model sentences.

mcqs.q: 'We are playing together' — We means ______.
mcqs.why: We means the speaker and others together, as in 'We are playing together.'

lessons.title: Objective Pronouns (p. 47)
lessons.notes_html:
Objective pronouns are used as objects of verbs or prepositions in sentences. Examples: He gave the book to me. Can you pass the salt to us? She told him the secret. I made a cake for her. They invited them to the party. Did you see it? He is talking about you. Object pronouns in the book's box: me, us, you, them, his, her, it. (Note: 'his' in the book's box is

a mistake - 'his' is a possessive word, not an object pronoun; the correct object pronoun is 'him', as used in the activity example 'The letter was written by him'. Flagged, not silently corrected in the list.)

mcqs.q: Objective pronouns are used as ______.
mcqs.why: Objective pronouns are used as objects of verbs or prepositions in sentences.

mcqs.q: 'He gave the book to ___.'
mcqs.why: The example is 'He gave the book to me,' so me is the objective pronoun.

mcqs.q: 'Can you pass the salt to ___?'
mcqs.why: The example says 'Can you pass the salt to us?' so us is the correct word.

mcqs.q: 'She told ___ the secret.' (a boy)
mcqs.why: The example is 'She told him the secret,' so him is the objective pronoun.

mcqs.q: 'I made a cake for ___.' (a girl)
mcqs.why: The example is 'I made a cake for her,' so her is the objective pronoun.

mcqs.q: 'They invited ___ to the party.'
mcqs.why: The example is 'They invited them to the party,' so them is correct.

mcqs.q: 'Did you see ___?' (a thing)
mcqs.why: The example is 'Did you see it?' so it is used for a thing as an object.

mcqs.q: 'He is talking about ___.'
mcqs.why: The example is 'He is talking about you,' so you is the objective pronoun.

mcqs.q: Which is an objective pronoun?
mcqs.why: Me is an objective pronoun from the book's box: me, us, you, them, her and it.

mcqs.q: In 'Please help me', 'me' comes after the ______.
mcqs.why: Me is the object of the verb help, showing objective pronouns follow verbs.

lessons.title: Activity — Use the following objective pronouns in your own sentences (him, her, me, you, us, them) (p. 47)
lessons.notes_html: Model sentences: 1. The letter was written by him. (given) 2. I gave a gift to her. 3. Please help me. 4. I will call you tomorrow. 5. The teacher told us a story. 6. We invited them to the party.

mcqs.q: 'The letter was written by ___.'
mcqs.why: The given model sentence is 'The letter was written by him' using him.

mcqs.q: 'I gave a gift to ___.' (a girl)
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'I gave a gift to her' using the objective pronoun her.

mcqs.q: 'Please help ___.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'Please help me' using the objective pronoun me.

mcqs.q: 'I will call ___ tomorrow.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'I will call you tomorrow' using the pronoun you.

mcqs.q: 'The teacher told ___ a story.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'The teacher told us a story' using the pronoun us.

mcqs.q: 'We invited ___ to the party.'
mcqs.why: The model sentence is 'We invited them to the party' using the pronoun them.

mcqs.q: Which sentence uses 'him'?
options: The letter was written by him
mcqs.why: The letter was written by him is the given correct model sentence in the activity.

mcqs.q: Who told us a story in the model sentence?
mcqs.why: The model sentence says the teacher told us a story, using us as object pronoun.

mcqs.q: In 'Please help me', who needs help?
mcqs.why: Me refers to the speaker, so 'Please help me' means the speaker needs help.

mcqs.q: Which list has only objective pronouns from the activity?
options: him, her, me, you, us, them
mcqs.why: The activity list is him, her, me, you, us and them, all objective pronouns.

lessons.title: Simple present verbs used to show habitual actions (p. 48)
lessons.notes_html: Read the following sentences: 1. She reads books every night. 2. They play soccer after school. 3. He brushes his teeth before bed. 4. We eat dinner together as a family.

mcqs.q: 'She ___ books every night.'
mcqs.why: The sentence is 'She reads books every night,' showing a habitual action.

mcqs.q: 'They ___ soccer after school.'
mcqs.why: The sentence is 'They play soccer after school,' a simple present habitual action.

mcqs.q: 'He ___ his teeth before bed.'
mcqs.why: The sentence is 'He brushes his teeth before bed,' showing his daily habit.

mcqs.q: 'We ___ dinner together as a family.'
mcqs.why: The sentence is 'We eat dinner together as a family' in simple present form.

mcqs.q: These sentences show ______ actions.
mcqs.why: Simple present verbs in this lesson show habitual actions done regularly.

mcqs.q: When does she read books?
mcqs.why: She reads books every night, which makes it a habitual, regular action.

mcqs.q: When do they play soccer?
mcqs.why: They play soccer after school, as given in the simple present examples.

mcqs.q: When does he brush his teeth?
mcqs.why: He brushes his teeth before bed, a habit shown in the lesson sentences.

mcqs.q: Who eats dinner together?
mcqs.why: We eat dinner together as a family, showing a family habitual action.

mcqs.q: Which verb is used with 'She' in the lesson?
mcqs.why: With She, the lesson uses reads: 'She reads books every night.'

mcqs.q: 'She ___ in her journal before sleep.'
mcqs.why: She writes in her journal before sleep is correct because She takes writes.

mcqs.q: 'We ___ our room every Saturday.'
mcqs.why: We clean our room every Saturday is correct because We takes the verb clean.

mcqs.q: When does he drink coffee?

mcqs.q: When do they watch movies?
mcqs.why: They watch movies on weekends, as given in the activity sentence.

mcqs.q: Where does she write before sleep?
mcqs.why: She writes in her journal before sleep, as given in the activity sentence.

mcqs.q: When do we clean our room?
mcqs.why: We clean our room every Saturday, as given in the fill-in-the-blank activity.

mcqs.q: What does he drink every morning?
mcqs.why: He drinks coffee every morning, which is the first sentence of the activity.

lessons.title: Long Vowel Phonemes (Sounds) (p. 48)
lessons.notes_html: Long vowel sounds can be represented by various spelling patterns in English. Examples: Long 'a' sound: cake (ai), rain (ai), play (ay). Long 'e' sound: bee (ee), seat (ea), key (ey). Long 'i' sound: bike (i-e), high (igh), pie (ie). Long 'o' sound: boat (oa), bone (o-e), go (o). Long 'u' sound: cube (u-e), mule (ue), blue (ue).

mcqs.q: Which word has a long 'a' sound?
mcqs.why: Cake is given as an example of the long 'a' sound in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Which word has a long 'a' sound with 'ai'?
mcqs.why: Rain has the long 'a' sound spelled with 'ai', as listed in the lesson.

mcqs.q: 'Play' has a long ______ sound.
mcqs.why: Play is listed under the long 'a' sound with the 'ay' spelling pattern.

mcqs.q: Which word has a long 'e' sound?
mcqs.why: Bee has the long 'e' sound spelled with 'ee', as given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: 'Seat' has a long 'e' sound spelled with ______.
mcqs.why: Seat is listed with the 'ea' spelling for the long 'e' sound in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Which word has a long 'i' sound?
mcqs.why: Bike has the long 'i' sound with the 'i-e' pattern, as given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: 'High' has a long 'i' sound spelled with ______.
mcqs.why: High is listed with the 'igh' spelling for the long 'i' sound.

mcqs.q: Which word has a long 'o' sound?
mcqs.why: Boat has the long 'o' sound spelled with 'oa', as given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: 'Cube' has a long ______ sound.
mcqs.why: Cube is listed under the long 'u' sound with the 'u-e' spelling pattern.

mcqs.q: Which word has a long 'u' sound?
mcqs.why: Blue has the long 'u' sound spelled with 'ue', as listed in the lesson.

mcqs.why: High is practised as a long 'i' word with bike and pie in the list.

mcqs.why: Boat, bone and go are practised together as the long 'o' sound words.

mcqs.q: Which three words are for long 'u'?
mcqs.why: Cube, mule and blue are practised together as the long 'u' sound words.

mcqs.q: 'Key' is practised for which sound?
mcqs.why: Key is in the long 'e' practise group with bee and seat in the activity.

mcqs.q: 'Pie' is practised for which sound?
mcqs.why: Pie is in the long 'i' practise group with bike and high in the activity.

mcqs.q: How many words are in the practise list?
mcqs.why: The list has 15 words: three each for long a, e, i, o and u sounds.

mcqs.q: What do we do in this activity?
mcqs.why: This activity is to practise long vowel phonemes with correct pronunciation.

lessons.title: Writing — Activity — Write down ten sentences of your daily routine (p. 49)

mcqs.q: What do I do in class?

mcqs.why: I eat dinner with my family, as written in the daily routine sentences.

mcqs.q: What is the last thing in the routine?
options: I go to bed early at night
mcqs.why: The last sentence is 'I go to bed early at night,' ending the daily routine.

lessons.title: A — Answer the following questions (p. 50)
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 1. Give example of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) kindness.
A: He fixed a bird's broken wing and looked after it until it could fly again, and in the Conquest of Makkah he forgave everybody.

Q: 2. Why did Abdul Qadir want to go to Baghdad?
A: To get more education.

Q: 3. What was the effect of telling the truth on the robbers?
A: The chief felt great shame, asked Allah for forgiveness, gave back all the snatched things to people and began to live a noble life.

Q: 4. How did Ali feel when his father told him that he would be alone?
A: He realized and felt ashamed.

Q: 5. What did Ali do after listening his father's advice?
A: He asked for forgiveness from the children and shared his bicycle, and they all rode it together.

mcqs.q: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) do for a bird?
mcqs.why: He fixed a bird's broken wing and looked after it until it could fly again, says the review answer.

mcqs.q: In the Conquest of Makkah, he:
mcqs.why: The review answer says in the Conquest of Makkah he forgave everybody, showing his great kindness to all.

mcqs.q: Why did Abdul Qadir want to go to Baghdad?
mcqs.why: Abdul Qadir wanted to go to Baghdad to get more education, as the review question answer clearly states.

mcqs.q: What did the chief of robbers feel after truth was told?
mcqs.why: The chief felt great shame, asked Allah for forgiveness and gave back all snatched things to people.

mcqs.q: After telling the truth, the robbers chief:
options: Gave back snatched things and lived noble life
mcqs.why: He gave back all snatched things and began to live a noble life after feeling shame and seeking forgiveness.

mcqs.q: How did Ali feel when his father said he would be alone?
mcqs.why: Ali realized and felt ashamed when his father told him he would be alone, says the review answer.

mcqs.q: What did Ali do after his father's advice?
mcqs.why: Ali asked forgiveness from children and shared his bicycle, and they all rode it together happily afterwards.

mcqs.q: Ali shared his:
mcqs.why: Ali shared his bicycle with the children after listening to his father's advice and asking for forgiveness.

mcqs.q: Telling the truth made the robbers:
mcqs.why: The effect of truth was that the chief repented and began to live a noble life with his robbers group.

mcqs.q: Abdul Qadir's story teaches us to:
mcqs.why: Abdul Qadir told the truth to robbers, and its good effect shows the lesson that we should tell the truth.

mcqs.why: Children play in the playground is the model sentence for the compound word playground in review section B.

mcqs.q: A rainbow appeared after:
mcqs.why: The model sentence says a rainbow appeared after the rain, using rainbow as the compound word example.

mcqs.q: The butterfly is described as:
mcqs.why: The model sentence says the butterfly is beautiful, describing the butterfly with the word beautiful in review.

mcqs.q: What does the firefighter do?
mcqs.why: The firefighter puts out the fire is the model sentence for firefighter, telling the firefighter's job clearly.

mcqs.q: Which compound word is a flower?
mcqs.why: Sunflower is a flower and a compound word made of sun and flower, used in the first model sentence.

mcqs.q: Which compound word is a person who fights fire?
mcqs.why: Firefighter is a person who puts out fires, and it is a compound word made of fire and fighter.

mcqs.q: Butterfly in the sentence is:
mcqs.why: The butterfly is beautiful is the model sentence, so beautiful describes how the butterfly looks in review.

lessons.title: Lesson text — Pollution (p. 54-55)
lessons.notes_html:
Pollution happens when harmful things, like smoke, trash, and chemicals, get into the air, water, or land. These harmful things can make the Earth dirty and cause problems for people, animals, and plants. Types of Pollution: 1. Air Pollution: Air Pollution happens when smoke and gases from cars, factories, and burning things go into the air. It can make the air dirty and hard to breathe. 2. Water Pollution: Water Pollution happens when dirty things like plastic, oil, or chemicals get into rivers, lakes, or oceans. This makes water unsafe for people and animals. 3. Land Pollution: Land Pollution happens when people throw trash or chemicals on the ground, making the land dirty and unsafe. 4. Noise Pollution: Noise Pollution happens when there is too much loud noise. It can hurt people's ears and make them feel upset. Problems caused by pollution: Health Problems: Pollution can make people sick. It can cause problems like coughing, breathing trouble, and even serious diseases. Harm to Animals: Animals can get hurt or even die if they eat trash or drink dirty water. Damage to the Earth: Pollution can harm plants and make the Earth dirty, which is bad for everyone. We can reduce pollution in many ways. First, we can use less plastic, reuse things like bottles and recycle paper and

cans to keep them out of the trash. We should also use less water by turning off the tap when it is not needed. Instead of driving cars, we can walk or ride a bike to keep the air clean. It is important to pick up trash and always use trash cans. Finally, we should plant trees, because trees help clean the air and give us oxygen. By doing these things, we can make our world cleaner and healthier. Pollution is bad for our health, animals, and the planet. But we can all help to reduce pollution by making small changes in our daily lives. If we all do our part, we can have a cleaner, safer world to live in.

After completing the unit, students will be able to: recognise 'stress' and 'intonation' patterns as used in statements and questions; distinguish between fact and opinion (for fiction and non-fiction text); identify and read the title of an article, book, or chapter; the function of captions and sub-heads; provide the missing letter in simple two/three syllable words; identify and recognize the rules for the use of 'a', 'an' and 'the' (e.g., The principal of my school, Mr. Aamir); use of a, an with countable and uncountable nouns; recognise past simple for completed actions/events in writing and speaking e.g., It rained in the morning; write an opening sentence to highlight the topic

sentence and introduce the setting in two to three sentences.

mcqs.q: What will you learn about stress and intonation in this unit?
options: To recognise their patterns in statements and questions
To write them in a poem only
To draw them in a picture
mcqs.why: The outcomes say students will recognise stress and intonation patterns as used in statements and questions.

mcqs.q: What two kinds of sentences will you learn to tell apart?
mcqs.why: The unit outcomes say students will distinguish between fact and opinion in fiction and non-fiction text.

mcqs.q: What will you learn to identify in a book?
options: The title of an article, book or chapter
mcqs.why: One outcome is to identify and read the title of an article, a book, or a chapter in this unit.

mcqs.q: What will you learn about captions and sub-heads?
mcqs.why: The outcomes include learning the function of captions and sub-heads in a book or article.

mcqs.q: What will you do with simple two or three syllable words?
options: Provide the missing letter in them
mcqs.why: An outcome of this unit is to provide the missing letter in simple two or three syllable words.

mcqs.q: Which three small words have rules you will learn?
mcqs.why: The unit teaches the rules for the use of 'a', 'an' and 'the' with different kinds of nouns.

mcqs.q: In the example 'The principal of my school, Mr. Aamir', which word is used before principal?
mcqs.why: The example in the outcomes uses 'The' before principal because it is a specific, known person.

mcqs.q: With which nouns will you learn to use 'a' and 'an'?
mcqs.why: The outcomes say students will learn the use of a and an with countable and uncountable nouns.

mcqs.q: Past simple is used for what kind of actions?
mcqs.why: Past simple is for completed actions or events, as in the example 'It rained in the morning'.

mcqs.q: What will you write at the start of a paragraph?
options: An opening sentence to highlight the topic and introduce the setting
A long list of new words
The last line of a story
mcqs.why: The writing outcome is to write an opening sentence that highlights the topic sentence and introduces the setting.

lessons.title: Poem — The Sunshine has a Pleasant Way, by Annette Wynne (p. 63)
lessons.notes_html: The sunshine has a pleasant way of shining on us all the day, it makes the little window bright, and fills the room with pretty light. It goes into the garden bed, and shines on every flower head; it warms each leaf and bud and seed till all the world is glad, indeed. It creeps into the children's faces and climbs into the highest places, it makes me want to work and sing and do my best in everything. I'm glad the sunshine comes each day to help me work and laugh and play; to keep the little window bright and fill the room with pretty light.

lessons.notes_html:
Haleem: Hey Umar, did you know that our class is starting a project on protecting the environment? (rising intonation) Umar: Really? That is

great! What's it all about? (falling intonation) Haleem: Well, we are going to learn about how important it is to take care of our planet. Umar: Right! I think everyone should do their part to protect the environment. Haleem: Yeah, like picking up trash in the schoolyard or using less plastic. Umar: And we can also plant trees. (rising intonation) Haleem: Exactly! Like, if everyone in our class plants a tree, imagine how many trees we could have! (rising intonation) Umar: And it's not just about trees. It's about taking care of animals, keeping our air and water clean. Haleem: Yeah! Together, we can protect our environment and make the world a better place for everyone. (rising intonation) Remember: Stress is the use of emphasis on the syllables or words in a sentence, while intonation is the rise and fall of voice when speaking.

lessons.title: Vocabulary and Grammar — Do you know? — Fact and Opinion (p. 67)
lessons.notes_html: Fact: A fact is a statement that can be verified or proven to be true. Opinion: An opinion is a personal belief, judgment, or viewpoint about something. Facts (from the poem): The sunshine shines on us all day. The sunshine makes the little window bright. The sunshine fills the room with light. The sunshine goes into the garden bed and shines on every flower head. The sunshine warms each leaf, bud, and seed. The sunshine creeps into the children's faces. The sunshine climbs into the highest places. The sunshine comes each day.

mcqs.why: An opinion is a personal belief, judgment, or viewpoint about something, unlike a proven fact.

lessons.title: Rules for using 'a,' 'an,' and 'the' (p. 69-70)
lessons.notes_html: 'A' and 'An': 'A' is used before words that begin with a consonant sound. Example: a fan, a book, a jar. 'An' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound. Example: an apple, an orange, an hour. 'The': 'The' is used before singular or plural nouns that are specific or known to the reader/listener. Examples: The book is on the table. The students are in my class. The sun is in the sky. With Uncountable Nouns: Uncountable nouns typically do not use 'a' or 'an' because they cannot be counted. Examples: milk, water, happiness, etc. 'the' can be used with uncountable nouns when referring to specific examples or quantities. Example: The milk is in the jug. The water is in the glass. With Countable Nouns: Countable nouns can be preceded by 'a' or 'an' when referring to a non-specific or singular example. Examples: a cat, an apple, a car, etc. When referring to a specific example, countable nouns use 'the.' Examples: the cat on the mat, the apple in the basket, etc.

mcqs.q: When do we use 'a' before a word?
mcqs.why: The rule says 'a' is used before words that begin with a consonant sound, like a fan or a book.

mcqs.q: When do we use 'an' before a word?
mcqs.why: The rule says 'an' is used before words that begin with a vowel sound, like an apple or an orange.

mcqs.q: Which is correct?
mcqs.why: Fan begins with a consonant sound, so we say a fan, as given in the examples for 'a'.

mcqs.q: Which is correct?
mcqs.why: Apple begins with a vowel sound, so we say an apple, as given in the examples for 'an'.

mcqs.q: When do we use 'the'?
mcqs.why: 'The' is used before singular or plural nouns that are specific or known to the reader or listener.

mcqs.q: When a countable noun is specific, we use ______.
mcqs.why: For a specific countable noun we use the, like the cat on the mat or the apple in the basket.

lessons.title: Student Learning Outcomes (p. 74)

lessons.title: Lesson text — Healthy Eating (p. 75-76)
lessons.notes_html:
Sadia was suffering from severe fever since last night. Her mother was very worried. She was repeatedly cold sponging Sadia so that Sadia's fever would go down. After some time, Sadia was feeling better. Her mother took Sadia to a doctor. The doctor checked her and asked, 'Dear daughter! what did you eat yesterday?' Sadia said that yesterday on her

way back from school, she had picked potato chips from a cart. The doctor said, 'Daughter! You know that most of the things made in the bazar are made of unhealthy material'. 'Some foods are good for our body, and some are not. Healthy foods help us grow strong and stay active. These are fruit, vegetables, milk, eggs and whole grains. Unhealthy foods can make us weak or sick. These are candy, chips, soda and fast foods. Dust and dirt on market items are birth place for germs. As soon as they enter the body, the growth of these germs increases and they attack different parts of the body. As a result the person becomes sick. The doctor suggested medicines to Sadia and explained, 'Daughter! People who take care of their health and hygiene, lead a better life in the society.' Sadia promised to take care of her health. Healthy Foods: Fruits, Vegetables, Fish, Egg, Milk, Meat, Nuts. Unhealthy Foods: Pizza, Burger, Noddles, Fries, Soft Drinks, Candies, Ice Cream.

mcqs.why: The story begins by saying Sadia was suffering from severe fever since last night.

mcqs.why: Her mother was repeatedly cold sponging Sadia so that her fever would go down.

mcqs.why: After Sadia felt better, her mother took Sadia to a doctor for a check-up.

mcqs.q: Which of these is an unhealthy food?

mcqs.why: The doctor says dust and dirt on market items are the birth place for germs.

options: Their growth increases and they attack the body
mcqs.why: The story says as soon as germs enter the body, their growth increases and they attack it.

options: To take care of her health
mcqs.why: Sadia promised to take care of her health after the doctor explained everything to her.

lessons.title: Lesson text — Safety Measures on Road (p. 86-88)
lessons.notes_html:
Teacher: Good morning, class! Today, we're going to discuss an important topic, 'Traffic rules and signs for our safety'. Can anyone tell me why it's important to follow traffic rules? Student A: Because they save us from accidents and keep everyone safe on the roads. Teacher: Exactly! Now, who can tell me what some common traffic signs mean? Student B: The stop sign means you have to come to a complete stop, right? Teacher: That's correct! And what about the speed limit signs? Student C: They tell us how fast we are allowed to drive in a particular area. (Speed limit sign shown: 70.) Teacher: Excellent! Now, let's talk about pedestrian crossings. What should drivers do when they see

someone crossing the road? Student D: They should stop and let the pedestrian cross safely. Teacher: Right again! Now, let's discuss some common mistakes that people make while driving. Can anyone think of a few? Student E: Using mobile phone while driving is a big one. It's really dangerous! Teacher: Absolutely! Using your phone while driving can lead to accidents. Remember, it's important to always keep your eyes on the road. Student F: What about not wearing seat belts? Teacher: That's another important point. Seat belts save lives, so it's important to fasten your seat belts every time you are in a vehicle. Student G: I heard that we should also use hand signals when riding bicycles. Is that true? Teacher: Yes, it is! Hand signals let other drivers know what you are planning to do. (Hand signal shown: Left Turn.) Student H: Thank you, teacher! I feel like I have learned a lot about traffic rules. Teacher: You are welcome! Remember, following traffic rules and signs is not just important for your safety. It is also important for the safety of everyone else on the road. We should be responsible citizens and follow traffic rules.

lessons.title: Student Learning Outcomes (p. 102)
lessons.notes_html: After completing the unit, students will be able to: interact by naming things, responding with simple sentences and asking questions about people and things in their immediate physical context; comprehend and respond to question words, e.g., what, where, when, who, why using pre and while reading strategies; read and follow simple instructions, e.g., in a recipe; recognise and locate some compound words from various text sources (e.g., butterfly, football, timetable, textbook, homework, classroom and whiteboard); recognise and use simple words that tell the position i.e. in, on, under, behind, next; identify and use simple sentences that show instructions, commands and requests; fill in missing information to complete a simple paragraph.

lessons.title: Poem — Twelve Months in a Row, by Annette Wynne (p. 103)
lessons.notes_html:
Twelve months in a row, use them well and let them go; welcome them without a fear, let them go without a tear. Twelve months in a year; greet the passing miracle, spring and summer beautiful, autumn, winter, gliding on, glorious seasons quickly gone. God's treasures in a row, take them, love them, let them go! (Pictures show the twelve months: January,

February, March, April, May, June, July, August, September, October, November, December.)

mcqs.q: Who wrote the poem 'Twelve Months in a Row'?
mcqs.why: The poem heading says 'Twelve Months in a Row, by Annette Wynne', so she is the poet.

mcqs.q: How should we use the twelve months?
mcqs.why: The poem says 'use them well and let them go', so we should use the months well.

mcqs.q: How should we welcome the months?
mcqs.why: The poem says 'welcome them without a fear', so we welcome them without fear.

mcqs.q: How should we let the months go?
mcqs.why: The poem says 'let them go without a tear', so we let them go without a tear.

mcqs.q: What should we greet in the poem?
mcqs.why: The poem says 'greet the passing miracle', speaking about the passing months and seasons.

mcqs.q: Which seasons are called beautiful in the poem?
mcqs.why: The poem says 'spring and summer beautiful', so spring and summer are called beautiful.

mcqs.q: How are the glorious seasons described?
mcqs.why: The poem says 'glorious seasons quickly gone', so the seasons go away quickly.

mcqs.q: What are God's treasures in a row in the poem?
mcqs.why: The poem calls the twelve months 'God's treasures in a row — take them, love them, let them go'.

mcqs.q: What should we do with God's treasures?
options: Take them, love them, let them go
mcqs.why: The last line says 'take them, love them, let them go' about God's treasures in a row.

mcqs.why: The months in order are January to December, and July comes right after June in the list.

lessons.title: Activity — Read the given process of making tea (p. 106)
lessons.notes_html: Recipe of Making Tea. Ingredients: Water, Tea leaves, Sugar, Milk. Process: 1. Take a cup of water and pour it into a kettle or pot. 2. Heat the water until it boils. 3. lessons.title: Oral Communication Skills — Practise the given (p. 107)
lessons.notes_html: dialogue in pairs Fatima: Aysha, have you seen my notebook anywhere? Aysha: I think it's on the table. Fatima: Oh, there it is! Thanks. Did you finish your homework? Aysha: Yeah, I just completed it. Do you need any help with yours? Fatima: No, I'm good, thanks. By the way, did you hear about the new cafe that opened near by? Aysha: Yeah, I heard about it. Have you been there yet? Fatima: Not yet, but I'm planning to go on this weekend. Do you want to come with me? Aysha: Sure, that sounds like fun! What time are you thinking of going? Fatima: Maybe around noon? Is it fine? Aysha: Yeah, that is fine. What kind of food do they have there? Fatima: I heard they have a variety of sandwiches, salads, and pastries. Plus, their coffee is also good. Aysha: Sounds delicious! I can't wait to try it. Do you know how to get there? Fatima: Yeah, it's just a few blocks from the park. We can walk there. Aysha: Perfect! I'm looking forward to it.

lessons.title: Words Showing Position (p. 109)
lessons.notes_html: The words that show position are called prepositions. Examples: In shows being inside something. The book is in the bag. On shows being on top of something. The pen is on the table. Under shows being beneath or below something. The cat is under the chair. Behind shows being at the back of something. The car is behind the house. Next to shows being adjacent to something. The lamp is next to the bed.

mcqs.why: The lesson example is 'The pen is on the table', so on is the correct position word.

lessons.title: Lesson text — Lost in the Jungle (p. 113-114)
lessons.notes_html:
One day, Ahmed and Imran's parents planned a trip to the jungle. The next day, they reached the jungle. They saw many fruit trees and beautiful flowers. They also saw nightingales, peacocks, and many other birds. In the evening, they all cooked dinner. After dinner, they all went into their tents. Imran and Ahmed couldn't sleep. They wanted to search for animals in the jungle. Although their parents did not allow them to

leave the tents. Still they went out to explore the jungle. As they walked, they felt they had gone quite far. When they tried to return, they couldn't remember where they came from. So, they sat down. Suddenly, they saw that an old man was passing by. The children greeted him: 'Assalam u Alaikum, uncle! We have lost our way. Can you help us?' The old man asked: 'How did you come here at this time of night and why?' Imran said: 'We went out to see animals and got lost away from our tent.' The old man said: 'Children! You should not have come without your parents.' Both of them said: 'Yes, we admit our mistake.' The old man said: 'Come, I'll take you to your parents.' They both walked with the old man and reached their parents, where their parents had been searching for them. They thanked the old man. The children asked their parents for forgiveness and promised not to repeat such an action in the future.

mcqs.why: The story begins by saying Ahmed and Imran's parents planned a trip to the jungle.

mcqs.why: The story says they planned one day and reached the jungle on the very next day.

mcqs.q: What did they see in the jungle?
mcqs.why: In the jungle they saw many fruit trees and beautiful flowers all around them.

mcqs.q: Which birds did they see?
mcqs.why: The story names nightingales, peacocks and many other birds that they saw in the jungle.

mcqs.why: After dinner, they all went into their tents to sleep for the night in the jungle.

mcqs.why: The story says their parents did not allow them to leave the tents at night.

mcqs.why: When they tried to return, they could not remember where they came from, so they sat down.

lessons.title: Vocabulary and Grammar — Joining Words (p. 119)
lessons.notes_html: Joining words or conjunctions connect words or sentences. Examples: and - It combines similar ideas. I like to read books and watch movies. but - It combines opposite ideas. I wanted to go to bazar, but it started raining. or - It presents choices. Would you like tea or coffee? so - It shows a result. It was raining, so we stayed indoors. because - It is used to give a reason for something. She didn't come to school because she was feeling sick.

mcqs.q: What do joining words do?
mcqs.why: Joining words, or conjunctions, connect words or sentences together in speaking and writing.

mcqs.q: Which joining word combines similar ideas?
mcqs.why: The lesson says 'and' combines similar ideas, as in reading books and watching movies.

mcqs.q: Which joining word combines opposite ideas?
mcqs.why: 'But' combines opposite ideas, like wanting to go to the bazar but rain starting.

mcqs.q: Which joining word presents choices?
mcqs.why: 'Or' presents choices, as in the question, 'Would you like tea or coffee?'

mcqs.q: Which joining word shows a result?
mcqs.why: 'So' shows a result: it was raining, so we stayed indoors and did not go out.

mcqs.q: Which joining word gives a reason?
mcqs.why: 'Because' gives a reason, like she did not come to school because she was sick.

mcqs.q: In 'I like to read books and watch movies', 'and' joins what?
mcqs.why: Reading books and watching movies are similar ideas joined by the word 'and'.

mcqs.q: Why did the girl not come to school in the example?
mcqs.why: The example says she did not come to school because she was feeling sick that day.

mcqs.q: What happened when it started raining in the 'so' example?
mcqs.why: The result of the rain was that we stayed indoors, shown by the joining word 'so'.

mcqs.q: Tea or coffee is an example of what?
mcqs.why: 'Would you like tea or coffee?' presents a choice between two things using 'or'.

mcqs.why: The 'or' model is the choice question, 'Would you like tea or coffee?' from the activity.

mcqs.why: Five joining words are given in the activity: and, but, so, or and because.

mcqs.why: The 'but' model joins wanting to play with the opposite idea that it started raining.

mcqs.why: The 'and' model sentence names apples and bananas as the two fruits the child likes.

lessons.title: Writing — Descriptive Writing (p. 120)
lessons.notes_html: In descriptive writing, we use adjectives (describing words) and sense words to describe persons, places or events. Example: The jungle was full of beautiful flowers. There were few dangerous animals. The night was bright because of the shining stars.

mcqs.q: In descriptive writing, we use what to describe?
mcqs.why: Descriptive writing uses adjectives, which are describing words, and sense words to describe.

lessons.title: Lesson text — The Golden Egg (p. 122)
lessons.notes_html: Once upon a time, a farmer had a hen that laid one golden egg every day. Every morning, he collected the egg and sold it. He earned enough to feed his family. But over time, he grew impatient. 'If this hen gives me a gold egg every day,' he thought, 'maybe she has lots of gold inside her! I could be rich now!' (While-reading: What do you think the farmer will do next? - He will kill the hen to get all the gold at once.) So one day, he killed the hen to open it and get all the gold at once. But inside, he found nothing. Not a single golden egg. Now the hen was gone, and with her, the steady daily gold. Moral: Don't be so greedy that you destroy what was giving you good things.

mcqs.why: The story begins: Once upon a time, a farmer had a hen.

mcqs.why: The story says he earned enough to feed his family from selling the eggs.

lessons.notes_html: Kamran: Dad, can I have 2000 rupees, please? Father: Sure, what do you need it for? Kamran: I need it for a school project. I have to buy some material. Father: How about we go to the store together? I'll buy what you need, and you can see how much everything costs. It's a good way to learn about spending money. Kamran: Yeah, that is good. Thanks, Dad. I love you. Father: Love you too, son. Let's go. Kamran: Okay.

lessons.title: Poem — Bed in Summer, by Robert Louis Stevenson (p. 129)
lessons.notes_html: In winter I get up at night and dress by yellow candle-light. In summer, quite the other way, I have to go to bed by day. I have to go to bed and see the birds still hopping on the tree, or hear the grown-up people's feet still going past me in the street. And does it not seem hard to you, when all the sky is clear and blue, and I should like so much to play, to have to go to bed by day?

mcqs.q: In winter, when does the poet get up?
