mcqs.q: By what light does the poet dress in winter?
mcqs.why: In winter the poet dresses by yellow candle-light because he gets up at night.

mcqs.q: In summer, when does the poet have to go to bed?
mcqs.why: In summer, quite the other way, the poet has to go to bed by day, says the poem.

mcqs.q: What does the poet see from bed in summer?
options: Birds still hopping on the tree
mcqs.why: From bed the poet sees the birds still hopping on the tree outside in daylight.

mcqs.q: What does the poet hear in the street?
mcqs.why: The poet hears the grown-up people's feet still going past him in the street.

mcqs.q: How is the sky in the poem?
mcqs.why: The poem asks if it does not seem hard when all the sky is clear and blue outside.

mcqs.q: What would the poet like so much to do?
mcqs.why: The poet says he should like so much to play instead of going to bed by day.

mcqs.q: Summer in the poem is 'quite the other way' to what?
mcqs.why: Summer is quite the other way to winter: in winter he gets up at night, in summer he beds by day.

mcqs.q: How does going to bed by day seem to the poet?
mcqs.why: The poet asks, 'And does it not seem hard to you,' to go to bed by day in summer.

lessons.title: Reading and Critical Thinking A — Read the poem (p. 130)
lessons.notes_html:
Q: 1. Describe the poet's routine in winter?
A: In winter he gets up at night and dresses by yellow candle-light.

Q: 2. How does the poet's routine differ in summer?
A: In summer, quite the other way - he has to go to bed by day.

Q: 3. What does the poet see from the bed during the day?
A: The birds still hopping on the tree.

Q: 4. How does the poet feel about having to go to bed during the day?
A: He feels it is hard - when all the sky is clear and blue and he would like so much to play, he has to go to bed by day.

Q: 5. What type of light does he use to dress in winter?
A: Yellow candle-light.

mcqs.q: What is the poet's routine in winter?
options: He gets up at night and dresses by candle-light
He goes to bed by day
mcqs.why: In winter he gets up at night and dresses by yellow candle-light, says the answer.

mcqs.q: How is the poet's routine different in summer?
options: He has to go to bed by day
mcqs.why: In summer, quite the other way, he has to go to bed by day instead of at night.

mcqs.q: What does the poet see from bed during the day?
options: The birds still hopping on the tree
mcqs.why: From bed during the day, the poet sees the birds still hopping on the tree outside.

mcqs.q: How does the poet feel about going to bed by day?
mcqs.why: He feels it is hard, when the sky is clear and blue and he wants to play outside.

mcqs.q: What type of light does he use to dress in winter?
mcqs.why: He dresses by yellow candle-light in winter, as both the poem and answer tell us.

mcqs.q: When does the poet get up in winter?
mcqs.why: The winter routine starts with getting up at night, not in the morning or at noon.

mcqs.q: What would the poet like to do instead of sleeping by day?
mcqs.why: He would like so much to play when the sky is clear and blue, instead of sleeping.

mcqs.q: What colour is the sky when he wants to play?
mcqs.why: The sky is clear and blue at the time he has to go to bed by day in summer.

mcqs.q: What are the birds doing on the tree?
mcqs.why: The birds are still hopping on the tree, which the poet can see from his bed.

mcqs.q: In summer, the poet goes to bed by what?
mcqs.why: The summer routine is the opposite: he has to go to bed by day in summer.

lessons.title: Reading and Critical Thinking B — Choose the correct option (p. 130-131)
lessons.notes_html:
1. The ______ is mentioned in the poem.

sunlight
moonlight
✓ candle-light
firelight

2. In summer, the poet has to go to bed ______.

at night
at dusk
✓ during the day
in the evening

3. The poet saw ______ while in bed during the day.

✓ birds hopping on the tree
cars passing by
stars in the sky
people sleeping

4. The poet hears the grown-up people's ______ going past him.

✓ feet
songs
hands
laughters

5. The poet expresses a desire to ______ instead of going to bed during the day.

study
eat
work
✓ play

mcqs.q: Which light is mentioned in the poem?
mcqs.why: The correct textbook option is candle-light, the yellow light used for dressing in winter.

mcqs.q: In summer, the poet has to go to bed when?
mcqs.why: The textbook answer says in summer the poet has to go to bed during the day.

mcqs.q: What did the poet see while in bed during the day?
mcqs.why: While in bed by day, the poet saw birds hopping on the tree outside his window.

mcqs.q: The poet hears the grown-up people's what going past?
mcqs.why: He hears the grown-up people's feet still going past him in the street outside.

mcqs.q: What does the poet wish to do instead of going to bed?
mcqs.why: The poet expresses a desire to play instead of going to bed during the day.

mcqs.q: Candle-light is used by the poet in which season?
mcqs.why: Candle-light is used in winter, when the poet gets up at night to dress in the dark.

mcqs.q: The birds in the poem are hopping on what?
mcqs.why: The birds are hopping on the tree, which the poet sees while lying in bed by day.

mcqs.q: Going past in the street are the grown-up people's what?
mcqs.why: Their feet going past in the street is the sound the poet hears from his bed.

mcqs.q: The poet must go to bed during the day in which season?
mcqs.why: It is in summer that the poet has to go to bed during the day, quite the other way.

mcqs.q: Instead of bed by day, the poet wants to do what?
mcqs.why: The desire expressed in the poem is to play outside under the clear blue sky.

lessons.title: Activity — The teacher or any student will recite the poem 'Bed in Summer' loudly, and the students clap on the words which rhyme (p. 132)
lessons.notes_html: Do you know? Prose is a normal writing in sentences and paragraphs (stories, articles). Poetry (Poem) is written in short lines, often has rhythm or rhyme, uses imagery. Drama (Play) is a writing for acting on stage, has characters and dialogues. (Recitation and clapping activity.)

mcqs.q: In this activity, students clap on which words?
mcqs.why: Students recite the poem loudly and clap on the words which rhyme with each other.

mcqs.q: What is prose?
options: Normal writing in sentences and paragraphs
mcqs.why: Prose is normal writing in sentences and paragraphs, like stories and articles we read.

mcqs.q: Stories and articles are examples of what?
mcqs.why: The lesson says prose includes stories and articles written in sentences and paragraphs.

mcqs.q: Poetry is written in what?
mcqs.why: Poetry, or a poem, is written in short lines and often has rhythm or rhyme in it.

mcqs.q: A poem often has rhythm or what?
mcqs.why: Poetry often has rhythm or rhyme and uses imagery, as the lesson's 'Do you know?' box says.

mcqs.q: Drama is writing meant for what?
mcqs.why: Drama, a play, is writing for acting on stage, with characters and dialogues in it.

mcqs.q: What does a drama or play have?
mcqs.why: A play has characters and dialogues, because it is written to be acted on a stage.

mcqs.q: Which text type uses imagery?
mcqs.why: The lesson says poetry uses imagery along with its short lines, rhythm and rhyme.

mcqs.q: Who recites the poem loudly in this activity?
mcqs.why: The teacher or any student recites 'Bed in Summer' loudly while others clap on rhymes.

mcqs.q: Clapping on rhyming words shows awareness of a poem's what?
mcqs.why: Clapping to rhymes shows awareness of the rhythmic structure of a poem or song.

lessons.title: Activity — Read the poem carefully and find rhyming words Rhyming Pair (p. 132)
lessons.notes_html:
1Night, Light (given)
2way, day
3see, tree
4feet, street
5you, blue
6play, day

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with 'night'?
mcqs.why: Night and light are the given rhyming pair at the start of the rhyming words activity.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with 'way'?
mcqs.why: Way rhymes with day, one of the rhyming pairs students find in the poem lines.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with 'see'?
mcqs.why: See and tree form a rhyming pair in the poem, from the birds hopping on the tree.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with 'feet'?
mcqs.why: Feet rhymes with street, from the grown-up people's feet going past in the street.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with 'you'?
mcqs.why: You and blue are a rhyming pair in the poem, in the line about the clear blue sky.

mcqs.q: Which word rhymes with 'play'?
mcqs.why: Play rhymes with day, the last rhyming pair listed from the poem 'Bed in Summer'.

mcqs.q: How many rhyming pairs are listed in this activity?
mcqs.why: Six rhyming pairs are listed, counting the given pair night-light and five more pairs.

mcqs.q: Which pair is given as the first example?
mcqs.why: Night and light is marked as the given pair, the first example for students to follow.

mcqs.q: 'Tree' rhymes with which word in the poem?
mcqs.why: Tree rhymes with see, from the line about having to go to bed and see the birds.

mcqs.q: 'Street' rhymes with which word in the poem?
mcqs.why: Street rhymes with feet, from the grown-up people's feet going past in the street.

lessons.title: Oral Communication Skills — Share your experience of a picnic orally as given in the following paragraph (p. 133)
lessons.notes_html:
We went to Bolan together. We splashed in the water, built castles with stones, and played cricket. Then, we had lunch with roast, sajji, and cold

drinks. We enjoyed a lot and took a lot of pictures to remember the fun day!

mcqs.q: Where did they go together for the picnic?
mcqs.why: The paragraph says, 'We went to Bolan together,' for the picnic day with friends.

mcqs.q: What did they do in the water at Bolan?
mcqs.why: At Bolan they splashed in the water, built castles and played cricket together.

mcqs.q: What did they build with stones?
mcqs.why: They built castles with stones during the picnic at Bolan, as the paragraph tells us.

mcqs.q: Which game did they play at the picnic?
mcqs.why: Playing cricket is one of the picnic activities named in the experience paragraph.

mcqs.q: What did they have for lunch?
mcqs.why: For lunch they had roast, sajji and cold drinks, says the picnic paragraph.

mcqs.q: Sajji was served with roast and what?
mcqs.why: Cold drinks were served at lunch along with roast and sajji at the Bolan picnic.

mcqs.q: Why did they take a lot of pictures?
mcqs.why: They took a lot of pictures to remember the fun day they spent together at Bolan.

mcqs.q: How did they feel about the picnic?
mcqs.why: The paragraph ends by saying they enjoyed a lot on the picnic day at Bolan.

mcqs.q: Castles at Bolan were built with what?
mcqs.why: The castles were built with stones found at Bolan, not with sand, wood or boxes.

mcqs.q: This lesson asks students to share an experience of what?
mcqs.why: Students share their experience of a picnic orally, following the Bolan paragraph model.

lessons.title: Activity — Read the above paragraph and discuss (p. 133)
lessons.notes_html: about a future picnic program at Bolan Discuss in class: a future picnic program at Bolan - when to go, what to take, what games to play, and what food to have. (Discussion activity.)

mcqs.q: The class will discuss a future picnic program at where?
mcqs.why: Students discuss a future picnic program at Bolan, based on the paragraph they read.

mcqs.q: What is the first thing to discuss about the future picnic?
mcqs.why: The discussion points are when to go, what to take, what games to play and what food.

mcqs.q: Which point is discussed for the future picnic?
mcqs.why: What to take is one of the four points listed for planning the future Bolan picnic.

mcqs.q: What will students plan about games?
mcqs.why: Students discuss what games to play at the future picnic, as one planning point.

mcqs.q: What food point is discussed?
mcqs.why: What food to have is the food point in the future picnic discussion at Bolan.

mcqs.q: How many planning points are listed for discussion?
mcqs.why: Four points are listed: when to go, what to take, what games to play and what food.

mcqs.q: This activity is based on reading which paragraph?
mcqs.why: Students read the Bolan picnic paragraph first and then discuss a future picnic program.

mcqs.q: The future picnic discussed is at the same place as the read picnic, which is?
mcqs.why: Both the read picnic and the future program discussed are at Bolan, the same place.

mcqs.q: 'When to go' is a question about what?
options: The time or day of the picnic
mcqs.why: 'When to go' asks about the time for the future picnic, the first discussion point.

mcqs.q: Students do this discussion where?
mcqs.why: The activity says to discuss the future picnic program at Bolan in class together.

lessons.title: Reading and Critical Thinking — Read the following (p. 134)
lessons.notes_html: paragraph and observe the use of transitional words showing sequence of events First, we got our material for picnic. Then, we drove happily by the Bolan River, singing. Next, we found a nice place and put our camp there. Finally, we went into the river, had fun, and laughed a lot.

mcqs.q: Which transitional word begins the picnic paragraph?
mcqs.why: The paragraph begins, 'First, we got our material for picnic,' showing the first event.

mcqs.q: What did they do first for the picnic?
mcqs.why: First, they got their material for the picnic, before driving happily by the Bolan River.

mcqs.q: Which word comes after 'First' in the sequence?
mcqs.why: The sequence taught is first, then, next, finally, so 'then' follows 'first' here.

mcqs.q: What did they do 'then' in the paragraph?
options: Drove happily by the Bolan River, singing
mcqs.why: Then, they drove happily by the Bolan River, singing, on their way to the picnic spot.

mcqs.q: Where did they drive happily, singing?
mcqs.why: They drove happily by the Bolan River, singing, as the second event in the sequence.

mcqs.q: What did they do 'next' in the paragraph?
options: Found a nice place and put their camp there
mcqs.why: Next, they found a nice place and put their camp there for the picnic by the river.

mcqs.q: Where did they put their camp?
options: At a nice place they found
mcqs.why: They put their camp at a nice place they found, as the 'next' event of the paragraph.

mcqs.q: What did they do 'finally' in the paragraph?
options: Went into the river, had fun and laughed
mcqs.why: Finally, they went into the river, had fun and laughed a lot, ending the sequence.

mcqs.q: Transitional words in this lesson show what?
mcqs.why: Transitional words show the sequence of events, the order in which things happened.

mcqs.q: How many transitional words are used in the paragraph?
mcqs.why: Four transitional words are used: first, then, next and finally, in that exact order.

lessons.title: Writing — Activity — Write down a simple paragraph (p. 134)
lessons.notes_html: using the words 'First, Then, Next, Finally' Model paragraph: First, I woke up early in the morning. Then, I took my breakfast and got ready for school. Next, I went to school and studied with my friends. Finally, I came back home and did my homework.

mcqs.q: What did the writer do first in the model paragraph?
options: Woke up early in the morning
mcqs.why: The model begins, 'First, I woke up early in the morning,' as the first daily event.

mcqs.q: What did the writer do 'then'?
options: Took breakfast and got ready for school
mcqs.why: Then, the writer took breakfast and got ready for school, says the model paragraph.

mcqs.q: What did the writer do 'next'?
options: Went to school and studied with friends
mcqs.why: Next, the writer went to school and studied with friends during the school day.

mcqs.q: What did the writer do 'finally'?
options: Came back home and did homework
mcqs.why: Finally, the writer came back home and did homework, ending the model paragraph.

mcqs.q: With whom did the writer study at school?
mcqs.why: The writer studied with friends at school in the 'next' part of the model paragraph.

mcqs.q: What meal did the writer take before school?
mcqs.why: The writer took breakfast and got ready for school in the 'then' part of the paragraph.

mcqs.q: What work did the writer do at home at the end?
mcqs.why: At the end, the writer came back home and did homework, as the model paragraph says.

mcqs.q: The model paragraph is written using which words?
mcqs.why: Students write the paragraph using the sequence words first, then, next and finally.

mcqs.q: When did the writer wake up?
mcqs.why: The writer woke up early in the morning, the first event in the model paragraph.

mcqs.q: Where did the writer go after getting ready?
mcqs.why: After breakfast and getting ready, the writer went to school in the model paragraph.

lessons.title: Activity — Read the following dialogues in the speech bubbles (p. 135)

options: Do you want to play with me?
mcqs.why: Salma asks, 'Do you want to play with me?' in the speech bubble at the park.

mcqs.q: How does Laila answer Salma?
options: Sure, Salma! I love to play with you
mcqs.why: Laila replies, 'Sure, Salma! I love to play with you,' accepting the invitation happily.

mcqs.q: Who speaks first in the park dialogue?
mcqs.why: Salma speaks first, inviting Laila to play with her in the park scene dialogue.

mcqs.q: Salma and Laila are what to each other?
mcqs.why: The scene introduces Salma and Laila as two friends together at the park.

mcqs.q: What does Laila love to do with Salma?
mcqs.why: Laila says she loves to play with Salma, in her reply in the speech bubble.

mcqs.q: The dialogue in this lesson is written in what?
mcqs.why: The dialogues are read in speech bubbles, the boxes that show what each person says.

mcqs.q: Laila's answer 'Sure' shows she is what?
mcqs.why: Saying 'Sure, Salma! I love to play with you' shows Laila is happy to play with her.

lessons.title: Activity — Fill in the speech bubbles [Scene: Two (p. 135)
lessons.notes_html:
friends, Salma and Laila, at the Railway Station]

mcqs.q: Where are Salma and Laila in this scene?

mcqs.q: What does Salma ask at the station?
mcqs.why: Salma asks, 'When will our train come?' in the model dialogue at the railway station.

mcqs.q: In how much time will the train come?
mcqs.why: Laila answers that the train will come in ten minutes, so they have a short wait.

mcqs.q: What does Laila suggest after her answer?
mcqs.why: Laila says, 'It will come in ten minutes. Let us wait here,' at the railway station.

mcqs.q: Who answers Salma's question about the train?
mcqs.why: Laila answers Salma, telling her the train will come in ten minutes at the station.

mcqs.q: The friends are waiting for what at the station?

mcqs.why: Students fill in the speech bubbles with a suitable dialogue for Salma and Laila.

mcqs.q: Waiting 'here' means waiting where?
mcqs.why: 'Let us wait here' means waiting at the railway station for the train to arrive.

mcqs.q: How many friends are in the station scene?
mcqs.why: Two friends, Salma and Laila, are in the railway station scene, like the park scene.

mcqs.q: Salma's question is about the coming of what?
mcqs.why: Salma asks when their train will come, because they are waiting at the railway station.

lessons.title: Activity — Read the dialogues [Scene: Salma throws (p. 136)

mcqs.q: What does Salma throw to Laila in this scene?

mcqs.q: What does Laila say back to Salma?
options: Thanks, Salma! Here, I'll throw it back to you
mcqs.why: Laila replies, 'Thanks, Salma! Here, I'll throw it back to you,' returning the ball.

mcqs.q: Who throws the ball back in the second scene?
mcqs.why: In the second scene, Laila throws the ball back to Salma, continuing their game.

mcqs.why: Salma says 'Nice catch' because Laila caught the ball well when it was thrown to her.

mcqs.q: Laila thanks Salma for what?
mcqs.why: Laila says 'Thanks, Salma!' in reply to Salma's praise for her nice catch of the ball.

mcqs.q: After thanking, what will Laila do?
options: Throw the ball back to Salma

mcqs.why: Two scenes are described: Salma throws and Laila catches, then Laila throws it back.

mcqs.q: The girls are playing with what in this activity?
mcqs.why: The whole dialogue activity is about the girls playing by throwing and catching a ball.

lessons.title: Activity — Write down dialogues in the following (p. 136)

mcqs.q: What does Salma say while playing?

mcqs.q: How does Laiba answer Salma?
options: Yes! Let us play again tomorrow

mcqs.q: When does Laiba want to play again?
mcqs.why: Laiba suggests playing again tomorrow, showing she also enjoyed playing with Salma.

mcqs.q: Students must write dialogues in what in this activity?
mcqs.why: Students write down dialogues in the speech bubbles for Salma and Laiba's happy play.

mcqs.q: Salma says the play is so much what?

mcqs.q: Who speaks second in the model dialogue?
mcqs.why: Laiba speaks second, answering Salma with 'Yes! Let us play again tomorrow.'

mcqs.q: Laiba's answer shows she wants to do what?
mcqs.why: By saying 'Let us play again tomorrow,' Laiba shows she wants to play again with Salma.

mcqs.q: The second friend in this scene is named what?

mcqs.q: Salma and Laiba continue doing what in the scene?
mcqs.why: The scene caption says Salma and Laiba continue playing happily in this last dialogue.

mcqs.q: Then the dog sat on what in the poem?

mcqs.q: What did the frog jump on in the poem?

mcqs.q: In the sun, what do we do in the poem?

mcqs.why: Eating a sweet bun is part of the sun, run and fun lines of the model poem.

lessons.title: Notes on the Book
lessons.notes_html:
Judgement calls and book errors (kept flagged, not silently fixed):

(1) Page 13: the book prints 'suflower' and 'betime' (for 'sunflower' and 'bedtime') and 'togather'/'wheter' (for 'together'/'whether') - corrected and flagged.

(2) Page 29: the book prints 'exited' in sentence 3 - corrected to 'excited' in the punctuated answer.

(3) Page 33, MCQ 4: 'connected' is a theme-based model answer, not a quoted line.

(4) Page 47: the book's object-pronoun box lists 'his' - 'his' is a possessive word, not an object pronoun; the correct form is 'him' (as in the activity example 'The letter was written by him') - flagged, list not silently altered.

(5) Page 65: the pictured title page differs from this book's own cover (pictured cover is red with a children's photograph; this book's cover is blue).

(6) Unit 7 title: the contents table says 'Eating Healthy' but the opener says 'Healthy Eating' - the opener title is used.

(7) Page 79 dialogue: speaker labels are Zohaib and Zain, but the lines address 'Faryal' and 'Najma' - reproduced as printed, mismatch flagged.

(8) Pages 88-89: the book writes 'Student 5' for the fifth student speaker (Student E, who highlights using a mobile phone while driving).

(9) Page 115, MCQ B1: the story says the parents planned 'a trip to the jungle'; the closest printed option, 'have a picnic in the jungle', is ticked.

(10) Page 124: the MCQ options are mislabelled (a), (b), (d), (d) - the third option is treated as (c).

(11) Page 135: the scene caption prints 'Tow friends' for 'Two friends' - corrected.

(12) Page 136: the second friend is spelled 'Laiba' in the scene caption but 'Laila' elsewhere - both spellings noted.

(13) Unit 9 MCQs (pages 104-105) are interpretive (theme, 'God's treasures', 'passing miracle') - the answers given are the best-supported readings of the poem.

(14) Contents-table page numbers drift: Revision 5-8 is actually pages 99-101 (not 102), Unit 9 starts page 102, Unit 10 starts page 112, Unit 11 starts page 121, Unit 12 starts page 128, Revision 9-12 is pages 138-139, and the Glossary is pages 140-148 - actual page footers were used throughout.
